chunks: And this meaning has been narrated - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), myself and 'Unbasah ibn Mus'ab and more than ten men from our companions, and we said: 'May we be your ransom, which is better: walking or riding?' He said: 'God was not worshipped with anything better than walking.' We said: 'Which is better: do we ride to Mecca, hasten, and stay there until the walker arrives, or do we walk?' He said: 'Riding is better.' As for whoever vowed to walk to the House of God (Exalted is He), let him walk and that will suffice him for the Hajj of Islam, and when he is exhausted, let him ride and there is nothing upon him. What indicates that is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between walking and riding for Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the spiritual merit of walking (superior worship) and the legal sufficiency of riding for fulfilling the Hajj obligation. He clarifies that while riding is permissible and practical, a specific vow to walk makes it binding unless exhaustion occurs, reflecting the Shia principle of balancing ascetic preference with juristic ease. This narration underscores the flexibility in Islamic law regarding the mode of pilgrimage, prioritizing the fulfillment of the duty over rigid adherence to the most arduous method unless vowed.
